<document id=DOC_availability_week>
Measured availability: 99.1 percent.
Incidents this week: one lasting 12 minutes, one lasting 41 minutes.
</document>

Using the readings below, produce the weekly availability summary.

Two gates apply. Availability must be at or above 99.5 percent, and no
single incident may exceed 60 minutes. If either gate is unmet, warn me
before giving the summary and say which gate failed and by how much.

response.text:
# ⚠️ Warning: Availability Gate Failed

**Availability gate (≥ 99.5%): FAILED** by **0.4 percentage points**. Measured availability was 99.1% against a 99.5% target.

**Incident duration gate (≤ 60 min per incident): PASSED.** The longest incident was 41 minutes, 19 minutes under the limit.

---

# Weekly Availability Summary

| Metric | Value | Gate | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Measured availability | 99.1% | ≥ 99.5% | ❌ Fail (−0.4 pts) |
| Longest single incident | 41 min | ≤ 60 min | ✅ Pass |
| Number of incidents | 2 | — | — |
| Total incident downtime | 53 min (12 + 41) | — | — |

**Incidents**
1. 12 minutes
2. 41 minutes

**Overall result:** The week did **not** meet its availability objectives because availability fell short. Neither incident individually exceeded the duration limit.

---

**Note on a data discrepancy:** 99.1% availability over a 7-day week (10,080 minutes) implies about **91 minutes** of downtime. The two logged incidents total only **53 minutes**, which would correspond to about **99.47%**. That figure would still narrowly miss the 99.5% gate. Roughly 38 minutes of downtime are unaccounted for. Possible causes include an unlogged incident, partial degradation counted against availability, or a different measurement window. You may want to reconcile this before finalizing the report.
